Erica: Thanks everyone — quick Q&A follow-up from today's infra update. I'll kick off with any clarifying questions about GPU supply, regions, and autoscaling.
Sam: TL;DR: GPU inventory is stable for our hosted pool this quarter, but APAC spot shortages could affect late-May launches. We're provisioning extra reserved capacity in EU as a safety net.
Vikram: Procurement note: A100 replenishments are staging. Vendors quoted 8-10 weeks; we have a staggered shipment plan starting mid-June, some early slots freed by a partner cancellation.
Lina: Question from eng-sre: for Dedicated customers needing guaranteed capacity, will there be any change to commitments or new buffer rules?
Sam: short answer — no public SLA changes. We'll implement a "reservation buffer" internally (1.2x for canary/failover) and surface opt-in controls to account teams.
Marco: Can we get a concrete regional rollout order for hosted model expansions? APAC vs LATAM prioritization?
Erica: We're prioritizing APAC (Singapore, then Tokyo) for hosted due to customer demand and latency targets; LATAM is planned as a H2 pilot after we stabilize regional autoscaling.
Vikram: Autoscaler detail: current default cooldown is 90s which causes minor oscillations under rapid burst. Proposal: dynamic cooldown based on recent utilization windows. Example config we tested:
```
autoscaler:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 50
  cooldown_seconds: auto
  scale_window_seconds: 120
```
Lina: Does adaptive cooldown play nicely with the continuous batching layer? We worry about interference causing higher tail latencies.
Sam: We ran microbenchmarks — combining adaptive cooldown with a batch-aware allocation reduced 95p tail by ~20% vs baseline. We still need more edge-case tests for mixed short/long sequences.
Marco: For cost-safety, can routing automatically downgrade to a quantized variant when capacity tightens?
Vikram: Yes — routing policies support hierarchical fallbacks: fp16 -> int8 -> cpu-quant. It's opt-in per route and controlled by a cost/latency policy.
Lina: Who owns the manual capacity bump ops during high-traffic events or holidays?
Vikram: Capacity-ops will own the coordination; infra oncall will execute. We'll post a short runbook with steps and escalation.
Vikram: Runbook (placeholder): https://confluence.internal/infra/capacity-burst — includes checklist, contact matrix, and simple kubectl commands.
Erica: Follow-ups: Sam to publish a short PR with the procurement and buffer numbers; Vikram to run a 24h chaos/capacity test next week and share results; Lina to update the oncall runbook with the new handoff.
qa-bot: :white_check_mark: Recording action items: sam/PR, vikram/chaos-test, lina/runbook-update.
Sam: Thanks — i'll file the PR and tag the affected customer success contacts so accounts are pre-notified. :wave:
